answer:
## ANSWER: N = 515

Genes significant (BH padj < 0.05) in at least one of the ΔlasI / ΔrhlI single mutants but NOT in the ΔlasIΔrhlI double mutant, under the pre-registered set operation **|(Sig_97 ∪ Sig_98) \ Sig_99|** with the primary model **~ Media + Strain**, Strain referenced to verbatim label "1". The model has actually been run (pure-Python DESeq2 port; ~30 s for all 7 models).

### Primary results (all 5828 supplied genes tested, no pre-filter, independent filtering off)
| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| Sig in strain 97 (assumed ΔlasI) vs 1 | 2802 |
| Sig in strain 98 (assumed ΔrhlI) vs 1 | 3321 |
| Sig in strain 99 (assumed double) vs 1 | 4255 |
| Union of singles | 4125 (3610 of these are also sig in the double) |
| **N = |(Sig_97 ∪ Sig_98) \ Sig_99|** | **515** |
| components (sum to 515) | lasI-only 259, rhlI-only 181, shared-by-both-singles 75 |
| stricter reading (sig in exactly ONE single, not double) — reported, not the answer | 440 |

### Sensitivity table (headline N side by side)
| model | genes | sig 97/98/99 | N | lasI-only / rhlI-only / shared |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| i primary ~Media+Strain | 5828 | 2802/3321/4255 | **515** | 259/181/75 |
| ii ~Replicate+Media+Strain | 5828 | 2860/3345/4289 | 519 | 266/176/77 |
| iii ~Strain only | 5828 | 1497/2146/3454 | **297** | 148/125/24 |
| iv primary + mean-count≥10 pre-filter (4 genes dropped) | 5824 | 2801/3321/4252 | 515 | 259/181/75 |
| v primary + DESeq2-style independent filtering | 5828 | 2802/3321/4255 | 515 | 259/181/75 (selected threshold = 0, i.e. filtering found no gain, so (v)≡(i)) |
| vi extra: same model, no dispersion shrinkage | 5828 | 2570/3074/4115 | 483 | 256/173/54 |
| vii extra: dispersions fully shrunk to the trend | 5828 | 3300/3853/4501 | 497 | 224/151/122 |

**Main caveat, flagged as requested:** every design that accounts for Media gives N = 483–519 (≈7% spread, including the dispersion-shrinkage variants), but the ~Strain-only model gives 297. Media explains 35.6% of the log-CPM variance (PC1) and is fully crossed with Strain, so dropping it removes signal-critical variance and deflates power; the pre-registered primary keeps it, so the reported answer is 515.

### Implementation verification (as requested in decision 1)
- Size factors: median-of-ratios from the 5824/5828 genes with all counts>0; range 0.767–1.394; Pearson r = 0.9223, Spearman r = 0.8741 vs library-size ratios, max |log(sf/libratio)| = 0.178 — i.e. ~1 with library size but deliberately deviating where composition differs, as intended. Estimator variants (all>0 genes / min≥5 genes / poscounts) agree to max |log ratio| < 0.001.
- Dispersion trend: disp(µ) = a1 + a2/µ + a3/µ², a1 = 0.01726, a2 = −2.292, a3 = 236.6; prior variance τ² = 1.0 (robust MAD variance of log(gene-wise/trend), capped at 1.0); Cox–Snell factor (n−1)/(n−p) = 1.167.
- Shrinkage behaves correctly: low-count genes are pulled to/past the trend (PA14_68150, mean 7.2: 0.0038 → 0.135, ratio 35.7; PA14_43405: 0.216 → 0.319), deep-count genes stay near their gene-wise value (PA14_41570, mean 293k: 0.0168 → 0.0148; PA14_71580: 0.0072 → 0.0071, ratio 0.99). Median shrink ratio per abundance bin: 1.55 (<20), 0.89 (20–100), 0.83 (100–1000), 0.83 (1000–5000), 0.81 (>5000).
- Independent model-free cross-check of dispersion magnitude from within strain×media cell variance (12 cells, n=3): quartiles 0.012 / 0.023 / 0.053 vs gene-wise median 0.0257 — same order, so dispersions are not under-estimated.
- Null calibration (strain labels permuted within media blocks, 2 reps): median p = 0.43–0.50, frac padj<0.05 = 0.0001–0.0011, and the headline statistic under the null is only 2–20 (vs 515 observed).
- BH implementation matches statsmodels `fdr_bh` to 2e-16; engine log2FC correlates 0.977–0.984 with the naive log2 ratio of mean normalised counts.
- One real bug was caught and fixed during development: an initially swapped NB log-likelihood term produced dispersions ~100× too small (p-values ~1e-269); the within-cell cross-check above is what exposed it.

### Representative genes driving N (locus tag, log2FC, padj in 97 / 98 / 99)
PA14_51350: +1.39 / 0.00 ; +0.31 / 1.3e-2 ; +0.09 / 0.50 (shared singles) · PA14_19590: −1.71 / 0.00 ; +1.49 / 4e-6 ; +0.46 / 0.16 · PA14_54830: +0.85 / 0.00 ; −0.19 / 0.20 ; −0.07 / 0.62 (lasI-only) · PA14_06320: +0.97 / 0.00 ; −0.22 / 0.21 ; +0.31 / 0.059 · PA14_13510: −0.07 / 0.58 ; +0.55 / 0.00 ; +0.18 / 0.10 (rhlI-only) · PA14_10680: +0.01 / 0.95 ; −0.52 / 1e-6 ; −0.13 / 0.23 (rhlI-only) — full top-25 in `results/representative_genes.csv`, all 515 in `results/primary_gene_table.csv` with a `class` column.
Effects are modest: median max|log2FC| among the sig singles of the N set is 0.34, and only 29/515 exceed |log2FC| = 1 — these are genes whose single-mutant perturbation is diluted below detection in the double, not large-magnitude genes.

### las/rhl loci: none of them are in N
The QS biosynthesis loci themselves are DE in the double as well, so they fall outside the answer set: candidate lasI locus PA14_53070 (log2FC −1.89 padj 5.6e-4 in 97; −0.61 padj 0.28 in 98; −1.85 padj 3.2e-4 in 99) and candidate rhlI-region loci PA14_71590 (ns in 97; −0.87 padj<1e-16 in 98; −1.23 padj<1e-16 in 99), PA14_71580 (−0.34 / −0.64 sig in 98 and 99). Hence N is composed of downstream/regulon genes with single-mutant-specific patterns.

### Genotype mapping (explicit assumption, verbatim labels kept everywhere)
The metadata contains only integer Strain labels **1, 97, 98, 99** — no "JBX1"/"lasI" strings exist in the inputs. Assumed key: **1 = JBX1 WT (reference), 97 = ΔlasI, 98 = ΔrhlI, 99 = ΔlasIΔrhlI**, inferred from mean normalised counts (results/genotype_marker_evidence.csv): las-dependent loci lost in 97 and 99 but WT-level in 98 (PA14_09440 69092/1266/54810/478; PA14_39945 75284/934/54363/308; PA14_53070 7504/502/4138/533), rhl-dependent loci lost in 98 and 99 but WT-level in 97 (PA14_72360 20596/21108/984/941; PA14_72370 14218/13737/757/728; PA14_10380 52900/56675/1467/599). Headline N is invariant to a 97↔98 swap; only the lasI-only (259) vs rhlI-only (181) breakdown depends on it.

### Limitations
1. Literal R/DESeq2 was impossible (no Rscript, no pydeseq2, no network); the port omits R-DESeq2 refinements — no Cooks-distance outlier replacement / coefficient tweaking, dispersion trend fitted to per-bin lower quartile with one refit iteration, τ² from a capped MAD estimate, Wald (not LRT) tests. Observed impact of the shrinkage choices on N is small (483–515), but absolute padj values are not guaranteed to match R DESeq2 digit-for-digit.
2. Genotype key is inferred, not supplied (documented above).
3. Per-cell n = 3, so Strain:Media interaction was deliberately not fitted; per-medium analyses would be underpowered (not run).
4. Overall DE counts are large (48–73% of genes per contrast) because the strain differences are genuinely large once Media is accounted for; a |log2FC| filter would shrink these drastically but was not part of the pre-registered criterion.
5. Independent filtering off in the primary run by design, so padj is computed over all 5828 tested genes.
